title: Mapping Interdisciplinary Heart Failure Care Pathways from the Perspectives of Patients and Stakeholders
summary:
- Background: Heart failure is a serious condition that, despite significant medical advances, continues to be associated with a high disease burden and considerable challenges in care across various disciplines. Over the course of their illness, patients come into contact with a wide range of healthcare providers, and shifting between inpatient and outpatient settings and areas of responsibility is characteristic of heart failure care. Scientific guidelines recommend structured and coordinated care approaches, but these are not yet widely implemented in Germany. 
- Research Question: How do patients and healthcare providers describe existing heart failure care pathways? 
- Methodology: Individual interviews will be conducted. Respondents will include both patients and healthcare providers involved in heart failure care.

interventions.name: Patients diagnosed with heart failure are interviewed once, in a one-on-one setting, about their experiences with heart failure care.
Stakeholders – that is, those involved in the care of people with heart failure – will be interviewed once, in a one-to-one interview, about their experiences with heart failure care.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Refers to the following group of patients: 
- Minimum age: 50 years
- patients diagnosed with heart failure
Exclusion criteria:
- if participants do not consent to an audio recording of the interview
